new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is penultimate; when the penultimate vowel is schwa (schwa being the only vowel allowed before the penult and restricted in the last two syllables), stress falls on the final syllable instead.
new_statements.exceptions: Schwa penult -> final stress. Note that Blust's 1971 Long Anap (Lepo' Sawa, same language) citation-form transcriptions mark stress mostly final even with full-vowel penults, and Blust 2013/2017 report final stress in citation forms vs penultimate in phrasal context for the area; Burkhardt's domain (citation vs phrase) is not visible in the snippet.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement for Lepu' Aga' (Lepo' Gah), an upper-Baram Highland Kenyah variety; snippet does not say whether citation forms or connected speech.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes Lepu' Aga' (= Lepo' Gah / Lepo' Aga), a Highland Kenyah variety of the upper Baram (Long Jeeh, Long Bela'ong, Long Silat, Long Sawan) and Tinjar (Long Teran), Sarawak, c. 1,000 speakers. SIL archives file it under Mainstream Kenyah [xkl]; Smith 2017 lists Lepo' Gah under Highland Kenyah (= Glottolog main1275). Glottolog main1275 has no separate dialect code for Lepo' Gah (its dialect nodes are lepo1241, umab1239 Uma Bem, umaj1239 Uma Jalam, umat1246 Uma Tau). Blust's 1971 notebook data are Long Anap = Lepo' Sawa, another main1275 variety. The Oxford Guide 2024 Kenyah stress snippet concerns Long Wat = Sebop (not main1275); Blust 2017's final-stress footnote concerns Lebu' Vu' (long1406).
